newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer shares fall on profits.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer shares fall on profits.

text.p: Shares in Marks and Spencer, Britain's biggest clothing retailer, were indicated lower on Tuesday amid disappointment over the group's half year profits.
The shares were down 12-1/2p to 496-1/2p by 0804 GMT in pre-market trade.

For the six months to September 28, the retailer posted pretax profits of 430.1 million, an increase of 11.6 percent over last year's 385.4 million stg. But some analysts had been expecting profits to rise by almost 20 percent.
The average of analysts' forecast was around 449 million stg.
The interim dividend payout was raised to 3.3p from 3.0p last year, in line with expectations.
Group sales rose 9.1 percent to 3,532.2 million stg and retail sales in the UK rose 8.4 percent. Meanwhile, financial activities contributed profits of 33 million, up 25 percent on last year.
M&S also said it planned to add 2,000 new jobs in Britain during the 1996/7 financial year, which would increase costs.
Analysts said the shares had fallen on disappointment that profits were 20 to 30 million stg below market expectations, although sales and revenues were strong.

They said profits were lower than forecast because of a 9.5 percent increase in costs during the first half. These came from investment in extra staff to boost customer service, which would pay dividends over the long term, they said.
"But the lower-than-expected profit will prompt downgrades," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
"We are reducing to 1,120 million stg from 1,160 million for the 1996/97 financial year," he said.
